seoTitle: How to Resize a TradingView Chart for Better Analysis
metaDescription: Learn how to resize your TradingView chart, zoom in and out, adjust price and time scale, and resize indicator panels for a cleaner layout.
intro: A chart that's too zoomed in, too small, or awkwardly scaled makes it harder to read price action clearly. This guide covers the basics of resizing a TradingView chart, including zoom controls, scale adjustments, and resizing indicator panels. It's aimed at beginners and active traders who want a more balanced, readable chart layout.

steps.heading: Zoom in and out using your mouse
steps.body: Use your mouse scroll wheel or the zoom controls on the chart to adjust how much price history is visible at once.

steps.heading: Adjust the price scale
steps.body: Drag the price axis on the right side of the chart to stretch or compress the vertical scale for better visibility.

steps.heading: Resize indicator panels
steps.body: Drag the borders between indicator panes to give more or less vertical space to specific indicators.

steps.heading: Adjust the time scale
steps.body: Drag the horizontal time axis at the bottom of the chart to control how much time is shown across the chart width.

steps.heading: Apply tips for a clean, balanced layout
steps.body: Aim for a scale that keeps price action easy to read without indicators feeling cramped or overly stretched.

faq.question: How do I quickly zoom back to the default chart view?
faq.answer: TradingView typically offers a reset or auto-scale option that returns the chart to its default zoom and scale settings.

faq.question: Why does my chart look too compressed or too stretched?
faq.answer: This usually happens when the price or time scale has been manually dragged out of proportion, which can be fixed by adjusting the scale directly.

faq.question: Can I resize individual indicator panes separately?
faq.answer: Yes, you can drag the border between panes to increase or decrease the space given to each indicator independently.

faq.question: Does resizing the chart affect the underlying data?
faq.answer: No, resizing only changes how the chart is displayed visually and doesn't affect the actual price or indicator data.
